report_meta.soc2_type_quote: SYSTEM AND ORGANIZATION CONTROLS (SOC) 2 TYPE 2 REPORT ON MANAGEMENT'S DESCRIPTION OF ITS Metabase Business Intelligence Platform

3.1.1.quote: During transport (exporting and importing, and backup) we encrypt using SSL & TLS. Connections from the Metabase app server to the database are encrypted using SSL & TLS.
3.1.1.note: Transit encryption is stated only as 'SSL & TLS'; the auditor 'Inspected the TLS configurations' (CC6.6.4/CC6.7.1, p36, no exceptions noted) but no TLS version number appears anywhere in the report, so no versioned dropdown option can be supported. Indicate: 'SSL/TLS (version not specified in SOC 2 report)'.

3.1.2.quote: The connection details to customer's DW is encrypted at row level with AES-256 CBC and we use SecretsManager to handle keys and associated metadata.
3.1.2.note: AES-256 (CBC) is explicitly named only for row-level encryption of customer data-warehouse connection details. The application database is 'encrypted at rest using AWS managed keys' (p11) and S3 buckets 'encrypted with SSE-KMS' (p13) with no algorithm named for those layers. CC6.7.2 'Customer data at rest is encrypted' tested with no exceptions noted (p36).

3.1.3.quote: All S3 buckets are encrypted with SSE-KMS and the Metabase encryption key which we create for every customer is saved in AWS Secrets Manager, with access restricted to key personnel
3.1.3.note: Backups go daily to AWS S3 ('Customer data is backed up daily to AWS S3', p12) and S3 is encrypted with SSE-KMS; backup transport uses SSL & TLS (p11). No cipher (e.g. AES-256) is named for backups, so no exact dropdown match. Indicate: 'AWS S3 SSE-KMS (algorithm not named in SOC 2 report)'.

3.1.4.quote: the Metabase encryption key which we create for every customer is saved in AWS Secrets Manager, with access restricted to key personnel via AWS IAM permissions.
3.1.4.note: Metabase creates a per-customer encryption key (customer-specific, generated by the subprocessor). Separately, the application database at rest uses 'AWS managed keys' (p11).

The entity uses an intrusion detection system to provide continuous monitoring of the entity's network and early detection of potential security breaches.

3.2.1.quote: Metabase is fully distributed across several countries with no physical office locations. All data is hosted by Amazon Web Services (AWS).
3.2.1.note: The report never names a hosting region or any EU/Europe data-location option ('EU', 'Europe', 'GDPR' appear nowhere); backups are 'replicated to another region' (p12) without saying which. Physical hosting is carved out to AWS as subservice organization: 'Our examination did not include the services provided by the subservice organizations' (p3-4) and 'AWS is responsible for restricting physical access to data center facilities' (p20). EU Access can therefore not be confirmed or denied from this report.

absent.reason: No statement on anonymization anywhere in the report ('anonym' has zero hits). Closest is an internal ETL 'that strips customer identifiable information from application databases to our redshift analytics warehouse' (p12), which is an internal de-identification pipeline, not a stated capability to anonymize personal data for customers — not inferred.
No mention of pseudonymization anywhere in the report ('pseudonym' has zero hits).
No TLS version (1.0/1.1/1.2/1.3) is stated anywhere; only 'SSL & TLS' (p11) and auditor inspection of 'TLS configurations' (p36).
